subject: humanities
passage: Swahili, spoken across much of East Africa, developed along a coast where traders from Arabia, Persia, India and, later, Portugal and Britain did business for centuries. Linguist Neema Mwakyusa traced the origins of 400 Swahili words related to trade and seafaring. She concluded that, in this vocabulary, words borrowed from Arabic outnumber the words borrowed from all other foreign languages combined.

data.title: Origins of 400 Swahili Words Related to Trade and Seafaring

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support Mwakyusa's conclusion?

choices.A: Words of Bantu origin, at 180, made up the largest single group among the 400 words in the sample.
choices.B: Arabic contributed 150 of the words, far more than the 20 words that came from Portuguese.
choices.C: Persian, Indian languages, Portuguese and English together contributed more of the words than Arabic did.
choices.D: Arabic contributed 150 of the words, while Persian, Indian languages, Portuguese and English together contributed 70.

explanation.why: Mwakyusa compares Arabic with all other foreign languages combined, so add up the bars for Persian (20), Indian languages (15), Portuguese (20) and English (15): 70 words. Arabic's 150 words are more than that total, and only one choice makes this comparison.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is true, but Bantu words are native to Swahili, not borrowed, so they are not part of Mwakyusa's comparison.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is true, but it compares Arabic with only one other language, not with all the other foreign languages combined.
explanation.C: Incorrect. These four sources together contributed 70 words, fewer than Arabic's 150, so this misreads the graph.
explanation.D: Correct. It compares Arabic with all the other foreign sources combined (20 + 15 + 20 + 15 = 70), which is the comparison the conclusion makes.
